# Envy and the neighbour

Envy is local. Nobody envies a medieval king or a billionaire on another continent with the bite that they envy a neighbour, a sibling or a colleague one desk away. The closer the model, the sharper the rivalry.

A thought from the street: when one house gets a new car, two more follow within the year. Nobody needed a car. Each neighbour read the other's wanting as proof that the object was worth having, and the imitation did the rest.

Envy is also ashamed of itself. People will admit to greed or anger before they admit to envy, which is why it hides behind talk of fairness.
